profile.summary: UCE (Universal Cell Embeddings) is a foundation model that maps single-cell RNA-seq profiles from any tissue or species into one shared embedding space. It takes raw counts plus protein language model embeddings of the genes, and outputs a cell embedding without any labelling, training or fine-tuning on the new dataset.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper Abstract and Fig. 1 legend; README.md: Output

summary_quotes.text: UCE can then map any cell
UCE takes as input (1) scRNA-seq count data; and (2) the corresponding protein embeddings, generated by a protein language model, ESM2
UCE’s universality means that new cells can be embedded with no data labelling, model training or fine-tuning.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: For each cell UCE draws a weighted sample of expressed genes (1,024 genes, with replacement). Each gene is represented by the ESM2 embedding of its protein product, so any protein-coding gene from any species can be represented from sequence. Genes are sorted by genomic location and grouped by chromosome with start and end tokens, then passed through a transformer. The cell embedding is the final-layer output of a CLS token. Training masks some expressed genes and asks a network, given the cell embedding and a gene's protein embedding, whether that gene was expressed.

quotes.text: UCE samples with replacement genes that were expressed, weighted by their level of expression.
Gene tokens are represented numerically by using ESM2 protein embeddings
The gene tokens are sorted by genomic location and grouped by chromosome.
The embedding of the cell is determined by taking the final layer output of a special CLS token that is appended before all the other tokens.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Two pretrained models are on Figshare: 4layer_model.torch, which the script uses by default, and 33l_8ep_1024t_1280.torch, the 33-layer model from the paper. Embeddings from the two are not compatible with each other. Figshare article 24320806 is at version 5. A result should name the model file, the Figshare version and the repository commit.

sections.title: Intended uses
sections.body: Zero-shot embedding of new single-cell datasets, for example to build integrated atlases or to transfer a cell type classifier to a new dataset. The authors used it to build the Integrated Mega-scale Atlas of 36 million cells.

quotes.text: We used UCE to create the Integrated Mega-scale Atlas, embedding 36 million cells
a cell type classifier trained to predict specific immune cell types can be seamlessly applied to a completely new dataset

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Zero-shot foundation model for single-cell gene expression that produces cell embeddings.

quotes.text: UCE’s universality means that new cells can be embedded with no data labelling, model training or fine-tuning.
implementation of the UCE model, to be used to embed individual anndata datasets

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Transformer over gene tokens built from ESM2 protein embeddings, ordered by chromosome and genomic position, with a CLS token for the cell embedding. The paper's model has 33 layers; a 4-layer model is also released.
facts.source_locator: Paper Results and Fig. 1 legend; README.md

quotes.text: UCE is a 33-layer model consisting of over 650 million parameters.
The gene tokens are sorted by genomic location and grouped by chromosome.
The script defaults to the pretrained 4-layer model.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: An h5ad file whose .X holds scRNA-seq counts and whose .var_names are gene names (not Ensembl IDs), plus the species name; protein embeddings for the species' genes.

quotes.text: The `.X` slot of the file should be scRNA-seq counts. The `.var_names` slot should correspond to gene names, *not ENSEMBLIDs*.
`species`: the species of the dataset you are embedding.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: The processed AnnData with UCE embeddings in .obsm["X_uce"], written to dir/{dataset_name}.h5ad.

quotes.text: Such a relationship requires that the number of genes sampled by UCE, 1,024, be relatively limited, especially given that individual cells might have more than 1,024 uniquely expressed genes.

limitations.text: Only 1,024 genes are sampled per cell, fewer than some cells express; the authors tie this to the quadratic cost of attention.

quotes.text: the quadratic increase in the runtime of transformers’ attention operations proportional to the number of tokens

limitations.text: The 4-layer and 33-layer models give incompatible embeddings, and the paper's datasets were embedded with the 33-layer model.

quotes.text: These datasets were embedded using the 33 layer model. Embeddings for the 33 layer model are not compatible with embeddings from the 4 layer model.
